policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'in the castle of the king's house' renders the construct chain the same way whether the qere carries the article (הַמֶּלֶךְ) or the ketiv omits it (מלך); English definiteness of 'the king's' does not expose the Hebrew article. The only note on the verse (Or, palace) is alternative_rendering, about the English for 'castle', and decides nothing here. Retain the qere base fallback.
